Andre Geim :: Academic career :: chunk_0002
After earning his PhD with Victor Petrashov,[[4]](#cite_note-bbcprofile-4) Geim worked as a research scientist at the Institute for Microelectronics Technology (IMT) at RAS, and from 1990 as a post-doctoral fellow at the universities of [Nottingham](/wiki/University_of_Nottingham "University of Nottingham") (twice), [Bath](/wiki/University_of_Bath "University of Bath"), and [Copenhagen](/wiki/University_of_Copenhagen "University of Copenhagen"). He said that while at Nottingham he could spend his time on research rather than "swimming through Soviet treacle", and determined to leave the Soviet Union.[[34]](#cite_note-PhysicsWorld-34)

He obtained his first tenured position in 1994, when he was appointed associate professor at [Radboud University Nijmegen](/wiki/Radboud_University_Nijmegen "Radboud University Nijmegen"), where he worked on [mesoscopic](/wiki/Mesoscopic_physics "Mesoscopic physics") [superconductivity](/wiki/Superconductivity "Superconductivity").[[35]](#cite_note-35) He later gained Dutch citizenship. One of his doctoral students at Nijmegen was [Konstantin Novoselov](/wiki/Konstantin_Novoselov "Konstantin Novoselov"), who went on to become his main research partner. However, Geim has said that he had an unpleasant time during his academic career in the Netherlands.

He was offered professorships at Nijmegen and [Eindhoven](/wiki/Eindhoven "Eindhoven"), but turned them down as he found the Dutch academic system too hierarchical and full of petty politicking. "This can be pretty unpleasant at times," he says. "It's not like the British system where every staff member is an equal quantity."[[34]](#cite_note-PhysicsWorld-34) On the other hand, Geim writes in his Nobel lecture that "the situation was a bit surreal because outside the university walls I received a warm-hearted welcome from everyone around, including Jan Kees and other academics."[[36]](#cite_note-NobelLecture-36) (Prof. Jan Kees Maan was the res

Nobara Kugisaki (釘崎 野薔薇, *Kugisaki Nobara*) is a first-year student at Tokyo Jujutsu High, trained by Satoru Gojo. She wields the Straw Doll Technique (芻霊呪法, *Sūrei Juhō*), attacking with nails and a hammer to channel two primary abilities: Resonance (共鳴, *Tomonari*), which links her strikes to a target's body or soul, and Hairpin (簪, *Kanzashi*), which detonates her nails with Cursed Energy. Originally from a rural village, she left to escape its oppressive environment. Partnered with Yuji and Megumi, she defeats the Death Painting brothers Eso and Kechizu. During the Shibuya Incident, Mahito gravely wounds her, leaving her comatose until the Shinjuku Showdown, where she assists Yuji's final attack on Sukuna with Resonance.

Macau is a [special administrative region of China](/wiki/Special_administrative_regions_of_China "Special administrative regions of China"), with executive, legislative, and judicial powers devolved from the [national government](/wiki/Government_of_China "Government of China").[[62]](#cite_note-CastellucciBLFundamentals-68) The [Sino-Portuguese Joint Declaration](/wiki/Joint_Declaration_on_the_Question_of_Macau "Joint Declaration on the Question of Macau") provided for economic and administrative continuity through the [handover](/wiki/Handover_of_Macau "Handover of Macau"), resulting in an executive-led governing system largely inherited from the territory's history as a Portuguese colony.[[63]](#cite_note-69) Under these terms and the "[one country, two systems](/wiki/One_country,_two_systems "One country, two systems")" principle, the [Basic Law of Macao](/wiki/Macao_Basic_Law "Macao Basic Law") is the regional [constitution](/wiki/Constitution "Constitution").[[64]](#cite_note-70) Because negotiations for the Joint Declaration and Basic Law began after transitional arrangements for Hong Kong were made, Macau's structure of government is very similar to Hong Kong's.[[65]](#cite_note-71)

In 1759, Ewing also became a pastor at the First Presbyterian Church, where Alison also had served as a pastor.[[2]](#cite_note-2) Ewing's sermons were popular with the general churchgoers and educated elites, according to a Presbyterian historian.[[3]](#cite_note-pcahist-3) A selection of his sermons was published in 1812.[[4]](#cite_note-4)

Ewing's senior role in the Presbyterian Church in Philadelphia earned him a position on the University of Pennsylvania's board of trustees from 1779 to 1802. He became the university's provost in 1780.[[1]](#cite_note-penn-bio-1)

Ewing's scientific pursuits included observing the 1769 [Transit of Venus](/wiki/Transit_of_Venus "Transit of Venus") from an observatory at the State House Yard and assisting with the routing of the boundary line for the state of Delaware and the path for the [Philadelphia and Lancaster Turnpike](/wiki/Philadelphia_and_Lancaster_Turnpike "Philadelphia and Lancaster Turnpike"). He joined the [American Philosophical Society](/wiki/American_Philosophical_Society "American Philosophical Society") in 1768 and served as the treasurer of the Corporation for the Relief of Poor and Distressed Presbyterian Ministers, one of the earliest American life insurance companies.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

Ewing traveled to Britain in 1773 to raise money for the Newark Academy in Delaware. During the trip, he was awarded an honorary doctor of divinity from the University of Edinburgh and met with a number of prominent Britons, including [Lord North](/wiki/Lord_North "Lord North"), who was the prime minister, and Dr. [Samuel Johnson](/wiki/Samuel_Johnson "Samuel Johnson"), the English writer.[[3]](#cite_note-pcahist-3)

Josh was born on 4 September 1992 in [Bermondsey, London](/wiki/Bermondsey,_London "Bermondsey, London"). He attended [Bexley Grammar School](/wiki/Bexley_Grammar_School "Bexley Grammar School") in [Welling](/wiki/Welling "Welling"), where he met future fellow Sidemen member [Tobi Brown](/wiki/TBJZL "TBJZL"). He claims to have had an interest in architecture in his early years, and used to love designing houses.[[5]](#cite_note-SidemenBook-5) As a child, Josh took dance lessons and competed in [street dance](/wiki/Street_dance "Street dance") performances.[[8]](#cite_note-8) His parents went through a divorce growing up, which he states led to him playing games. He claims to have played *Call of Duty* in his room for 8 hours, because he wanted an escape from the stress of his parents' divorce.[[9]](#cite_note-:2-9)[[10]](#cite_note-10) In the Netflix documentary, *The Sidemen Story*, Josh had mentioned that he suffered from [anxiety](/wiki/Anxiety "Anxiety").[[11]](#cite_note-11)

He later attended [Ravensbourne University](/wiki/Ravensbourne_University_London "Ravensbourne University London") and earned an upper second honours degree in digital film production.[[5]](#cite_note-SidemenBook-5) Before getting into content creation, Josh tried working in a bank in London with his father, who was a banker himself, but left soon after. He also had a week-long stint at the [Sky Sports](/wiki/Sky_Sports "Sky Sports") studio.[[5]](#cite_note-SidemenBook-5)

In 2009, Josh created his first YouTube channel, *Zerkaa*,[[12]](#cite_note-12) to which he primarily uploaded video game content from games like *[Call of Duty](/wiki/Call_of_Duty "Call of Duty")* and *[FIFA](/wiki/FIFA_(video_game_series) "FIFA (video game series)")*.[[13]](#cite_note-FIFAGambling-13) He has subsequently launched six more solo YouTube channels — namely *ZerkaaPlays, ZerkaaReacts, ZerkaaLive, ZerkaaActuallyPlays, ZerkaaGuesses, and ZerkaaCards.*

Although very small amounts of berkelium were possibly produced in previous nuclear experiments, it was [first intentionally synthesized](/wiki/Timeline_of_chemical_element_discoveries "Timeline of chemical element discoveries"), isolated and identified in December 1949 by [Glenn T. Seaborg](/wiki/Glenn_T._Seaborg "Glenn T. Seaborg"), [Albert Ghiorso](/wiki/Albert_Ghiorso "Albert Ghiorso"), [Stanley Gerald Thompson](/wiki/Stanley_Gerald_Thompson "Stanley Gerald Thompson"), and [Kenneth Street Jr.](/wiki/Kenneth_Street_Jr. "Kenneth Street Jr.") They used the 60-inch [cyclotron](/wiki/Cyclotron "Cyclotron") at the [University of California, Berkeley](/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley "University of California, Berkeley"). Similar to the nearly simultaneous discovery of [americium](/wiki/Americium "Americium") (element 95) and [curium](/wiki/Curium "Curium") (element 96) in 1944, the new elements berkelium and [californium](/wiki/Californium "Californium") (element 98) were both produced in 1949–1950.[[26]](#cite_note-Thompson1950-26)[[35]](#cite_note-35)[[36]](#cite_note-E97-36)[[37]](#cite_note-37)[[38]](#cite_note-38)

For commercial use, varieties with a minimum stem length of 30 centimetres (12 in) are sought, making them ideal for cut flowers. Florists require blooms that only open when they reach the retail outlet. For garden plants the objectives are to continually expand the colour palette and to produce hardy forms, and there is a particular demand for miniature varieties. The cultivars so produced tend to be larger and more robust than the wild types.[[6]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHanks2002[httpsbooksgooglecombooksid4_kH_BffGDgCpgPA1_Hanks,_"The_biology_of_''Narcissus''"],_pp._1–29-7) The main species used in breeding are *[N. bulbocodium](/wiki/Narcissus_bulbocodium "Narcissus bulbocodium")*, *[N. cyclamineus](/wiki/Narcissus_cyclamineus "Narcissus cyclamineus")*, *[N. jonquilla](/wiki/Narcissus_jonquilla "Narcissus jonquilla")*, *[N. poeticus](/wiki/Narcissus_poeticus "Narcissus poeticus")*, *[N. pseudonarcissus](/wiki/Narcissus_pseudonarcissus "Narcissus pseudonarcissus")*, *[N. serotinus](/wiki/Narcissus_serotinus "Narcissus serotinus")* and *[N. tazetta](/wiki/Narcissus_tazetta "Narcissus tazetta")*.[[183]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOkuboSochacki2012[httpsbooksgooglecombooksid5B-ucdbgA3wCpgPA105_105]-186)

*Narcissus pseudonarcissus* gave rise to trumpet [cultivars](/wiki/Cultivars "Cultivars") with coloured tepals and corona, while its subspecies *N. pseudonarcissus* subsp. *bicolor* was used for white tepaled varieties. To produce large cupped varieties, *N. pseudonarcissus* was [crossed](/wiki/Hybrid_(biology) "Hybrid (biology)") with *N. poeticus*, and to produce small cupped varieties back crossed with *N. poeticus*. Multiheaded varieties, often called "Poetaz" are mainly hybrids of *N. poeticus* and *N. tazetta*.[[6]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHanks2002[httpsbooksgooglecombooksid4_kH_BffGDgCpgPA1_Hanks,_"The_biology_of_''Narcissus''"],_pp._1–29-7)

fanoutqa_028533.t: World War II :: Background :: European treaties :: chunk_0007
fanoutqa_028533.x:
World War II :: Background :: European treaties :: chunk_0007
The United Kingdom, France and Italy formed the [Stresa Front](/wiki/Stresa_Front "Stresa Front") in April 1935 in order to contain Germany, a key step towards [military globalisation](/wiki/Military_globalization "Military globalization"); however, that June, the United Kingdom made an [independent naval agreement](/wiki/Anglo-German_Naval_Agreement "Anglo-German Naval Agreement") with Germany, easing prior restrictions. The Soviet Union, concerned by Germany's [goals of capturing vast areas of Eastern Europe](/wiki/Drang_nach_Osten "Drang nach Osten"), drafted a treaty of mutual assistance with France. Before taking effect, though, the [Franco-Soviet pact](/wiki/Franco-Soviet_Treaty_of_Mutual_Assistance "Franco-Soviet Treaty of Mutual Assistance") was required to go through the bureaucracy of the League of Nations, which rendered it essentially toothless.[[21]](#cite_note-23) The United States, concerned with events in Europe and Asia, passed the [Neutrality Act](/wiki/Neutrality_Acts_of_the_1930s "Neutrality Acts of the 1930s") in August of the same year.[[22]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchmitz2000124-24)

Hitler defied the Versailles and [Locarno Treaties](/wiki/Locarno_Treaties "Locarno Treaties") by [remilitarising the Rhineland](/wiki/Remilitarisation_of_the_Rhineland "Remilitarisation of the Rhineland") in March 1936, encountering little opposition due to the policy of [appeasement](/wiki/Appeasement "Appeasement").[[23]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAdamthwaite199252-25) In October 1936, Germany and Italy formed the [Rome–Berlin Axis](/wiki/Axis_powers "Axis powers"). A month later, Germany and Japan signed the [Anti-Comintern Pact](/wiki/Anti-Comintern_Pact "Anti-Comintern Pact"), which Italy joined the following year.[[24]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShirer1990298–299-26)

fanoutqa_005749.t: Essential amino acid :: Essentiality in humans :: chunk_0002
fanoutqa_005749.x:
Essential amino acid :: Essentiality in humans :: chunk_0002
Of the twenty amino acids common to all life forms (not counting [selenocysteine](/wiki/Selenocysteine "Selenocysteine")), humans cannot synthesize nine: [histidine](/wiki/Histidine "Histidine"), [isoleucine](/wiki/Isoleucine "Isoleucine"), [leucine](/wiki/Leucine "Leucine"), [lysine](/wiki/Lysine "Lysine"), [methionine](/wiki/Methionine "Methionine"), [phenylalanine](/wiki/Phenylalanine "Phenylalanine"), [threonine](/wiki/Threonine "Threonine"), [tryptophan](/wiki/Tryptophan "Tryptophan") and [valine](/wiki/Valine "Valine"). Additionally, the amino acids [arginine](/wiki/Arginine "Arginine"), [cysteine](/wiki/Cysteine "Cysteine"), [glutamine](/wiki/Glutamine "Glutamine"), [glycine](/wiki/Glycine "Glycine"), [proline](/wiki/Proline "Proline") and [tyrosine](/wiki/Tyrosine "Tyrosine") are considered **conditionally essential**,[[8]](#cite_note-8) which means that specific populations who do not synthesize it in adequate amounts, such as newborn infants and people with diseased livers who are unable to synthesize cysteine, must obtain one or more of these conditionally essential amino acids from their diet.[[9]](#cite_note-9)[[10]](#cite_note-10) For example, enough arginine is synthesized by the urea cycle to meet the needs of an adult but perhaps not those of a growing child. Amino acids that must be obtained from the diet are called **essential amino acids**.

[Eukaryotes](/wiki/Eukaryotes "Eukaryotes") can synthesize some of the amino acids from other [substrates](/wiki/Substrate_(biochemistry) "Substrate (biochemistry)"). Consequently, only a subset of the amino acids used in protein synthesis are [essential nutrients](/wiki/Essential_nutrient "Essential nutrient").
